subject: Bad fit of measurement model between SPSS AMOS and R lavaan

messages.author: 2537dd572df56eb7
messages.subject: Bad fit of measurement model between SPSS AMOS and R lavaan
parts:
Hello,

I am doing a moderated mediation SEM for my PhD and am experiencing some problems. My supervisor and I are using the same dataset and the same MM, but the results do not fit. SPSS produces goodness of fit values that are, well, good, and lavaan does not.

I am almost certain I messed up the code somewhere. My CFI is borderline (.903) and RMSEA is too high (.083). However, I also noticed that my number of parameters is 59 and my supervisor's is 61, my df = 194 and my supervisor's = 192. I am sure there lieth the problem, but I am stuck with fixing it. Can anyone help, please?

Here is the code:
m_whole_c<-"
      SPOT=~SPOT1+SPOT2+SPOT3+SPOT4
      MOTIV=~MOTIV1+MOTIV2+MOTIV3+MOTIV4+MOTIV5
      WORK=~WORK1+WORK2+WORK3
      EC=~SPOT+MOTIV+WORK
     
      EAg=~EA1+EA3+EA4+EA5
     
      ESEg=~ESE1+ESE2+ESE3
     
      EA_2=~EA2
     
      Spol=~SPOL
      Druz_podj=~DRUZ_BINAR
      "

whole_m<- lavaan::cfa(m_whole_c, data = df, sample.cov = T)
summary(whole_m, fit.measures = T, standardized = T)

Thank you if you can help out.

Best,
Janez

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Bad fit of measurement model between SPSS AMOS and R lavaan
parts:
SPSS doesn't do SEM. Do you mean Amos?

Look at the parameters one at a time. Your model must have parameters in it that your supervisor's model does not.  Perhaps lavaan is adding some correlations between exogenous variables that Amos doesn't. Amos is sometimes weird about constraining means when you don't expect it to.

Also:

      Spol=~SPOL
      EA_2=~EA2
      Druz_podj=~DRUZ_BINAR

I don't see either of these variables anywhere else in the model. I think that having two different variables have the same name, but one upper case and one lower case is technically OK, but if it was me, I'd immediately get confused. Similarly, EA2 and EA_2 - I might as well make a typo now. :) 

(I get confused easily, so I put quite a lot of effort into ensuring my code is as un-confusing as it can be. A couple of things I do:

 - make it very clear what's latent, and what's not.
- spac out my code to make it easier to read, e.g. 

      SPOT_latent =~ SPOT1 + SPOT2 + SPOT3 + SPOT4
)
